events.title: Granada Massacre
events.description: A mob stormed the royal palace in Granada, killed the Jewish vizier Joseph ibn Naghrela, and slaughtered much of the city's Jewish population.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest episodes of anti-Jewish violence in medieval Iberia. It also marked the end of a period of notable Jewish influence in the Taifa of Granada.

events.title: Gadsden Purchase Signed
events.description: U.S. ambassador James Gadsden signed a treaty with Mexico. It transferred roughly 30,000 square miles of land in what is now southern Arizona and New Mexico to the United States.
events.significance: The purchase set the southern border of the contiguous United States. It also secured a viable route for a southern transcontinental railroad.

events.title: Rudyard Kipling Is Born
events.description: Joseph Rudyard Kipling was born in Bombay (now Mumbai), British India. He became one of the best-known English-language writers of his era, famous for The Jungle Book and Kim.
events.significance: In 1907 Kipling became the first English-language writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature. His work still shapes how people picture the British Empire and its legacy.

events.title: Soviet Union Formally Established
events.description: The First Congress of Soviets of the USSR approved the treaty that united the Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian and Transcaucasian republics into one state.
events.significance: The USSR became one of the world's two superpowers and a central player in the 20th century. It lasted until its dissolution in 1991.

events.title: Saddam Hussein Executed
events.description: Former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein was hanged in Baghdad. He had been convicted by the Iraqi High Tribunal for crimes against humanity.
events.significance: His execution ended a dictatorship of more than two decades. It remains a deeply divisive moment in Iraq's modern history.
